access_note: Free after accepting the Deltares licence; a demonstration version can be downloaded, and operational users receive the full version after signing the licence. Support and maintenance agreements and training are paid services.
description: Delft-FEWS is Deltares' flood forecasting and early warning platform: a data management and model integration system that brings together observations, weather forecasts and hydrological and hydraulic models to run operational forecasts. Deltares, an independent Dutch applied research institute for water, subsurface and infrastructure, develops it for forecasting centres managing floods, droughts, reservoirs, water supply and water quality. It is not itself a model: models such as Delft3D, HEC-RAS or MIKE 11 are connected through adapters or the General Adapter, and scripts in Python or R can run inside workflows. It imports over 100 data formats, exposes a Web Services API, is configured in XML and supports seven interface languages. As of 2024 Deltares reports use in nearly 70 countries, and releases come twice a year. Access: free to use after accepting the licence; a demo can be downloaded and operational users get the full version after signing; the code is open software but not open source, and support, training and service packages are paid. Caveats: configuration takes training and effort, the core source is not public, and forecasts depend on the models and data each centre connects. Simulation uses: real-time flood and drought forecasting, early warning, reservoir operation, emergency response and operational digital twins of river and drainage systems. Related records: HEC-RAS (model-hec-ras) and ANUGA (model-anuga), and the reference paper by Werner and others in Environmental Modelling and Software (2013).
